title: Ordinary balanced reduction under an invertible multiplication map
statement: Let C be a site with the sheafification assumptions of [def-pbc-successive-derived-scalar-normalization-data], let R to B to S be morphisms of commutative ring sheaves, and let p and N be presentations and normalized scalar-extension data as in that definition. Suppose the normalized ordinary counit B tensor_R Res(S) to Res(S) is invertible, where Res(S) is the restriction of the coefficient unit along B to S. Then restriction from B to R followed by extension from R to S is naturally isomorphic to extension from B to S. The isomorphism sends every scalar-first pure section s tensor x to s tensor x. No flatness is assumed. The tensor and restriction conventions are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tags 03EK and 05V4; displayed balanced tensor cancellation followed by the multiplication isomorphism.

proof.text: Define the canonical S-linear map as the inverse normalized composition comparison followed by scalar extension of the phi-adjunction counit. The normalized inverse composition formula, naturality of the ordinary unit and the triangle identity show that it sends each s tensor x to s tensor x.

Identify restricted scalar extension of M with M tensor the restricted coefficient unit. Before sheafification this is the identity on the tensor abelian group followed by tensor commutation. Restriction commutes with sheafification because the underlying abelian sheafification is the same. These identifications send s tensor x to x tensor s.

Apply [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation-independent] in the inverse direction to send x tensor s to x tensor (1 tensor s). Tensor the assumed multiplication isomorphism with M, then invert the preceding restricted-extension identification. This is an isomorphism after restriction. Its section formula agrees with the canonical S-linear map from step 1: the counit sends 1 tensor s to s by the adjunction triangle. Pure tensors generate after sheafification, so the maps agree. Restriction reflects isomorphisms, hence the canonical map is invertible. Naturality gives the required natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03EK and 05V4, sheafified balanced tensor argument; explicit canonical-map normalization by ordinary adjunction.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinary_flatCoefficientComparison
    (p : ∀ {A A' : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}} (a : A ⟶ A'), Presentation a)
    (N : Normalization p) {R B S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}} (φ : R ⟶ B) (ψ : B ⟶ S)
    (hμ : IsIso ((N.ordinaryAdjunction φ).counit.app
      ((restriction ψ).obj (unit (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))))) :
    ∃ o : restriction φ ⋙ (p (φ ≫ ψ)).ordinary ≅ (p ψ).ordinary,
      ∀ (M : Modules B) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj.obj U) (x : M.val.obj U),
        (o.hom.app M).val.app U
          (sectionTensor (p (φ ≫ ψ)) ((restriction φ).obj M) U s x) =
            sectionTensor (p ψ) M U s x
